_comment: Octail curated egg (plan §6.4). Octail's own, following no-more-room-in-hell.json and the pelican-eggs steamcmd base script (games-steamcmd, MIT licence), on Octail's source image (32-bit libraries). App 346680 (anonymous SteamCMD, Linux build) with the game folder (bms) fixed. Octail adds the black-mesa tags, Source RCON on the game port with a generated password hidden from customers, the Players tab (source preset) and the Steam query (A2S) for player counts, a max players setting (-maxplayers), an optional Game Server Login Token (+sv_setsteamaccount only when one is set), start detection by the Steam ID line or the Steam connection line with the UDP game port as a fallback (ready after 60 s), generic UDP idle sleep (off until staff enable it per server), the say broadcast, the update before start (AUTO_UPDATE, on by default), an optional beta branch, a starter server.cfg, install sandbox defaults and resource hints, and makes the install fail when SteamCMD didn't download the server. SteamCMD is retried up to 3 times: its first run on a fresh install often fails with "Missing configuration"; the SteamCMD download times out and retries instead of hanging the install. The disk hint is 50 GB: the Steam depots install about 31 GB (30.1 GB main depot 346681, 0.8 GB shared 221145, 0.1 GB Linux 346683) and download 13.5 GB (12.9 GB plus 0.6 GB; SteamCMD API, 2026-10-16), which SteamCMD stages next to the install before moving the files into place, so a fresh install peaks at about 44.5 GB; 20 GB and 40 GB disks both ended in SteamCMD state 0x202 (not enough disk) on node1 (2026-10-13). The install checks the free space first and stops with "Not enough disk space" below 45 GB, and prints the free disk after the download. SteamCMD exits 0 even when an install failed (Missing configuration), so its retry loop counts a run as done only on SteamCMD's "Success! App" line.
name: Black Mesa: Deathmatch
author: octail@meowgafactory.com
description: Black Mesa is the fan-made, Valve-approved remake of Half-Life on the Source engine; its dedicated server hosts Black Mesa Deathmatch.

installation.script:
#!/bin/bash
# Black Mesa Dedicated Server (app 346680) Installation Script
#
# Server Files: /mnt/server
# Based on the pelican-eggs steamcmd base script (games-steamcmd, MIT licence).
#
# Variables
# SRCDS_APPID - 346680 (Black Mesa Dedicated Server, anonymous)
# SRCDS_BETAID - an optional beta branch

## The Black Mesa dedicated server installs anonymously
STEAM_USER=anonymous

## Octail: SteamCMD refuses to start an app (state 0x202) when the free space is short of the install plus its
## download, which it stages next to the install (steamapps/downloading) before moving the files into place.
## Checked here first, with a clear message: the game files are 31 GB (30.1 GB depot 346681, 0.8 GB shared 221145, 0.1 GB Linux
## 346683) and their download 13.5 GB (Steam's depot manifests, 2026-10-16): 44.5 GB at the peak of a fresh install.
## A 40 GB disk got state 0x202 on node1 (2026-10-13).
MIN_FREE_MB=46080
free_mb=$(df -Pm /mnt/server | awk 'NR == 2 { print $4 }')
if [[ -n "${free_mb}" && "${free_mb}" -lt "${MIN_FREE_MB}" ]]; then
    echo "Not enough disk space: the install needs at least ${MIN_FREE_MB} MB free on the server's disk and it has ${free_mb} MB. Ask for a disk of 50 GB, then reinstall."
    exit 1
fi

## download and install steamcmd (only the 3 MB archive goes through /tmp; SteamCMD, its caches and its download
## staging live on the server's disk)
cd /tmp || exit 1
mkdir -p /mnt/server/steamcmd
## Octail: time out and retry instead of hanging the install when the download stalls
curl -fsSL --connect-timeout 30 --max-time 300 --retry 3 -o steamcmd.tar.gz https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/client/installer/steamcmd_linux.tar.gz || { echo "Could not download SteamCMD; try reinstalling."; exit 1; }
tar -xzvf steamcmd.tar.gz -C /mnt/server/steamcmd
rm -f steamcmd.tar.gz
mkdir -p /mnt/server/steamapps # Fix steamcmd disk write error when this folder is missing
cd /mnt/server/steamcmd || exit 1

# SteamCMD fails otherwise for some reason, even running as root.
# This is changed at the end of the install process anyways.
chown -R root:root /mnt
export HOME=/mnt/server

## install game using steamcmd
beta=()
[[ -z ${SRCDS_BETAID} ]] || beta=(-beta "${SRCDS_BETAID}")
## Octail: SteamCMD's first run often fails with "Missing configuration"; try up to 3 times
for steamcmd_try in 1 2 3; do
    if ./steamcmd.sh +force_install_dir /mnt/server +login "${STEAM_USER}" +app_update "${SRCDS_APPID}" "${beta[@]}" validate +quit 2>&1 | tee /tmp/steamcmd.log && grep -q "Success! App '" /tmp/steamcmd.log && ! grep -q "ERROR! Failed to install app" /tmp/steamcmd.log; then break; fi
    echo "SteamCMD did not finish (attempt $steamcmd_try of 3)"
done
echo "octail: free disk after the download: $(df -Pm /mnt/server | awk 'NR == 2 { print $4 }') MB"

## set up 32 bit libraries
mkdir -p /mnt/server/.steam/sdk32
cp -v linux32/steamclient.so ../.steam/sdk32/steamclient.so

## set up 64 bit libraries
mkdir -p /mnt/server/.steam/sdk64
cp -v linux64/steamclient.so ../.steam/sdk64/steamclient.so

## Octail: fail the install when SteamCMD didn't download the server
if [[ ! -f "/mnt/server/srcds_run" || ! -d "/mnt/server/bms" ]]; then
    echo -e "\nSteamCMD failed to install the Black Mesa dedicated server; try reinstalling."
    exit 1
fi

## A server.cfg to start from; an existing one is kept
if [[ ! -f "/mnt/server/bms/cfg/server.cfg" ]]; then
    mkdir -p /mnt/server/bms/cfg
    printf '%s\n' 'hostname "Black Mesa server on Octail"' 'sv_password ""' 'sv_lan 0' > /mnt/server/bms/cfg/server.cfg
fi

## install end
echo "-----------------------------------------"
echo "Installation completed..."
echo "-----------------------------------------"

variables.name: App ID
variables.description: The Steam app id of the Black Mesa Dedicated Server.

variables.name: Map
variables.description: The first map, for example dm_bounce, dm_crossfire, dm_stalkyard or dm_undertow.

variables.name: Steam Game Server Login Token
variables.description: Optional: a Steam Game Server Login Token (app id 362890, the Black Mesa game) so the server keeps the same Steam ID and shows in the server list reliably. Generate one at https://steamcommunity.com/dev/managegameservers

variables.name: RCON Password
variables.description: Source RCON password. Octail generates one when the server is created, keeps it from customers and sends console commands over RCON.

variables.name: Beta branch
variables.description: An optional Steam beta branch; empty for the public build. Reinstall after changing it.

variables.name: Auto-update server
variables.description: Check for a server update with SteamCMD at every start (1 on, 0 off).
